text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when its motor neuron stops firing, so acetylcholine is broken down by acetylcholinesterase at the neuromuscular junction and the fibre is no longer excited. Calcium is then pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum by SERCA, and tropomyosin re-blocks the myosin-binding sites on actin. The team note is incorrect: skeletal muscle is driven by motor neurons through the neuromuscular junction, not by sensory neurons bypassing it.

CONFIDENCE: 85
